mechanism_narrative: Increasing GDP (GDPC1) reflects strong economic activity, which positively impacts S&P 500 returns as corporate earnings are expected to rise.
failure_condition: S&P 500 returns do not increase despite GDP growth over a 60-day horizon in majority cases.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 4% signals a strong labor market, boosting consumer spending and corporate profits.
failure_condition: S&P 500 returns are negative when UNRATE drops below 4% over a 20-day horizon.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous growth in industrial production (INDPRO) and housing starts (HOUST) indicates strong economic expansion, positively influencing S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: No positive correlation between combined growth of INDPRO and HOUST and S&P 500 returns over 20 days.

mechanism_narrative: Rising federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) during a tightening cycle may lead to decreased corporate borrowing and lower equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 returns remain positive despite FEDFUNDS increase in a tightening cycle.

mechanism_narrative: Rising consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) may lead to inflationary pressures, prompting monetary tightening and negative S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 returns do not decline despite CPIAUCSL increases over 20 days.

mechanism_narrative: A significant increase in housing starts (HOUST) above 1500 units signals strong demand, positively impacting S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 returns are negative when HOUST exceeds 1500 units over 5 days.

mechanism_narrative: Combined growth in employment (PAYEMS) and decline in unemployment (UNRATE) signals a robust labor market, boosting S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: No positive correlation between labor market improvements and S&P 500 returns over 20 days.

mechanism_narrative: Growth in real retail sales (RSAFS) during late-cycle expansion indicates strong consumer spending, positively influencing S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 returns are negative despite RSAFS growth in late-cycle expansion.
